correctness.rationale: For all positive couplings and time constants on c=1+tau_x/tau_y<1+b, exact substitution gives an invariant affine center plane, dv/dt=(u-v)/tau_y and du/dt=u/tau_y-bv/tau_x, hence the harmonic oscillator with positive omega squared. The full affine Jacobian factors into a purely imaginary pair and a strictly stable pair, so every periodic orbit staying in the closed active region lies in that plane. Its u oscillates symmetrically with amplitude K rho, giving a necessary and sufficient threshold K rho<=min(p,q/sigma); continuity of ReLU validates tangency. An exact disk-to-ellipse Jacobian yields the projected and intrinsic areas, and the two competing positive linear thresholds cross uniquely at r=sigma. The analytical all-parameter proof is supplemented by a passed SymPy identity check and the exact rational example (tau_x,tau_y,b,a12,a21,s1,r)=(1,4,1/2,1,25/16,1,5/4), radius 2 sqrt(2)/11 and area 8 pi/121.

value.rationale: At the center/grazing bifurcation already identified by the originating model, the exact size of the neutrally periodic admissible set and its dependence on neuronal input balance are naturally motivated quantities. The theorem gives a complete closed-activity periodic classification and the sharp unique ratio r=sqrt(a21/a12) that maximizes the active center island, with two-threshold grazing precisely at that ratio and quadratic area loss near both feasibility limits. This is not merely the known center eigenvalue or a textbook harmonic-period computation; it resolves how the natural switching boundaries restrict the actual nonlinear system and supplies a precise parameter design rule.
